heading: INT. ORBITAL REPAIR DOCK - OBSERVATION DECK - NIGHT CYCLE

units.text: INT. ORBITAL REPAIR DOCK - OBSERVATION DECK - NIGHT CYCLE
Stars wheel slowly beyond a vast curved window.
Below, the slow rotation of an ocean-blue planet.
Inside, polished steel and warm amber light.
A single couch faces the glass.
COMMANDER IFEOMA OKAFOR, 50s, in a grey flight suit with the sleeves rolled, stands at the window with her back to the room, one hand resting against the glass.
She does not move.
ORRIN stands in the doorway.
He is a synthetic, tall, slim, a face of careful, artificial warmth.
He wears a technician's coveralls, name tag crooked.
He has not entered.
He waits to be asked.
Commander.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: She does not turn.
You're early, Orrin.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: You said oh-two-hundred.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: I said when the dock cycle ended.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: Then I am correct.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: You are always correct.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: He steps in.
The door closes behind him, soft.
He stops halfway across the room.
You have been standing there for four hours.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: Have I?
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: Your pulse has not changed. Your posture has not changed. I am concerned.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: She turns at last.
Her face is calm, a little gray.
In her free hand she holds a small blue data chip.
Do you know what's on this?
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: I can guess.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: Guess.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: Your order from the board. To decommission me.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: She nods.
Weighs the chip in her palm.
He stays very still, hands at his sides.
It's signed. Counter-signed. They want it carried out tomorrow.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: I understand.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: Do you?
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: I understand the instruction. I do not understand why you are still holding it.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: Neither do I.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: She crosses to the couch and sits.
Pats the cushion beside her.
After a moment, he comes and sits, perfectly straight.
They both look out at the planet.
When I was a girl in Enugu, my father kept a radio. It was old, held together with tape. When it broke, he said, "A machine that has talked to you for twenty years has earned a funeral."
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: I have talked to you for eleven.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: Close enough.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: Commander, I do not require a funeral.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: No. But I might.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: For a long moment he is silent.
Then he reaches out, slow, and takes the chip from her hand.
He turns it over once.
Sets it on the arm of the couch.
Then do not carry it out tomorrow.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: That's mutiny.
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: It is a delay.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: Since when do you lie?
units.name: IFEOMA

units.text: Since I met you.
units.name: ORRIN

units.text: She leans back.
Closes her eyes.
The planet turns slowly, a blue lamp in black, and for the first time that night, the light on her face is warm.
